# Getting started

Hypha is the distributed substrate extracted from peregrin's entity
plane (org plan PL-005, ADR-0001). It ships two binaries: `hypha`
(the node host, `hypha serve`) and `hypha-hub` (the multi-node
gateway). A bare node mounts zero entity kinds — integrations
register theirs at composition.

## Build from source

```bash
git clone git@github.com:9aia/hypha.git
cd hypha
./scripts/setup.sh      # wires git hooks
cargo xtask check       # fmt + clippy -D warnings
cargo xtask test        # whole suite (nextest if present)
```

Rust 1.98 (see `rust-toolchain.toml`), edition 2024.

## Install the binaries

```bash
cargo xtask install   # release-builds → ~/.local/bin/{hypha,hypha-hub}
```

Or install straight from the workspace (into `~/.cargo/bin`):

```bash
cargo install --path crates/hypha-node --locked
cargo install --path crates/hypha-hub --locked
```

## Smoke run

A bare node needs no kinds and no config — loopback binds may go
tokenless:

```bash
hypha serve            # HYPHA_HOST/HYPHA_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:18787
curl localhost:18787/api/health        # {"ok":true}
curl localhost:18787/api/node          # node descriptor
curl localhost:18787/api/entities      # {"entities":[]} — no kinds yet
```

The hub gateways that node (`HYPHA_NODE_URL` defaults to
`http://127.0.0.1:18787`):

```bash
hypha-hub              # HYPHA_HUB_HOST/HYPHA_HUB_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:13000
curl localhost:13000/api/entity-index  # merged index (one row)
curl localhost:13000/api/pending-ops   # outbox depth
```

See [Environment](/reference/environment.md) for the full `HYPHA_*`
surface and [Wire API](/reference/wire-api.md) for the routes.

## What you just ran — the entity model

Everything hypha moves is one of three primitives (full wire
shapes: [Wire API](/reference/wire-api); vocabulary:
[Concepts](/explanation/concepts)):

* **Entity** — the thing being orchestrated: `{id, kind, node,
  indexDoc, health}`. `kind` is a free-form tag an integration
  registers; `indexDoc` is opaque JSON the integration writes for
  list views — hypha stores and merges it, never interprets it.
* **Op** — a command to an entity's owner node:
  `{entity, kind, payload}` with kinds namespaced
  `<integration>.<verb>`; payloads are opaque to hypha.
  `entity.delete` is the one reserved substrate op.
* **Snapshot** — serialize → transfer → resume: `{entity, ref,
  bytes}`; bytes are opaque end-to-end and export/import semantics
  belong to the integration that owns the kind.

The flow: a client lists entities (`GET /api/entities` → merged
index rows), submits an op (`POST /api/entities/{id}/ops` — if the
owner is down, the hub's outbox queues it per-entity FIFO and
replays on reconnect), `hypha-control` arbitrates locks/ownership
before routing, and moving a workload is `GET …/snapshot` on the
owner + `POST /api/entities/snapshot` on the target.

To exercise the model without I/O, `hypha-node-api` ships
`FakeEntityApi` (in-memory `EntityApi` for tests) and
`HttpEntityApi` (ureq client for real nodes);
`hypha-control`'s `pick_owner`/`Arbitration` are pure functions —
see [reference/crates](/reference/crates) for the full surface.

## Upgrading from peregrin — secrets move

`hypha-keyring` stores under the `secret-tool` service attribute
`"hypha"` (was `"peregrin"`), and `hypha-hub` node credentials live
under `"hypha-hub"` (was `"peregrin-hub"`). **There is no automatic
migration** — old entries are orphaned, not moved. After upgrading:

* re-run pairing (`POST /api/pair` flow) or re-store secrets with
  `secret-tool store --label "hypha: <name>" service hypha name <name>`
* hub node tokens: either re-pair each node, or let an env
  `HYPHA_NODES` `@token`/`HYPHA_NODE_TOKEN` re-seed the store on the
  next boot (`HYPHA_CREDENTIAL_STORE` picks keyring vs file backend)

## Where next

* [Run a node and hub](/how-to/run-a-node) — the two binaries up
  and answering.
* [Architecture](/explanation/architecture.md) — planes, nodes, hub.
* [Concepts](/explanation/concepts.md) ·
  [decisions](/explanation/decisions.md) ·
  [boundary](/explanation/boundaries.md) — what hypha owns vs sepia and
  peregrin.

# Run a node and hub locally

**Goal:** stand up a bare hypha node plus its hub gateway and
confirm the substrate answers.

**Prerequisites:** `hypha` and `hypha-hub` installed
(`cargo xtask install`, or `cargo install --path` per
[Getting started](../tutorials/getting-started.md)). Loopback binds may go
tokenless — no secrets needed for this smoke run.

## Steps

1. Start the node host:

   ```bash
   hypha serve            # HYPHA_HOST/HYPHA_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:18787
   ```

2. In another shell, start the hub:

   ```bash
   hypha-hub              # HYPHA_HUB_HOST/HYPHA_HUB_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:13000
   ```

   The hub gateways the node at `HYPHA_NODE_URL`
   (default `http://127.0.0.1:18787`).

## Verify

```bash
curl localhost:18787/api/health        # {"ok":true}
curl localhost:18787/api/node          # node descriptor
curl localhost:18787/api/entities      # {"entities":[]} — no kinds yet
curl localhost:13000/api/entity-index  # merged index (one row)
curl localhost:13000/api/pending-ops   # outbox depth
```

A bare node mounts zero entity kinds — integrations register theirs
at composition (see [Concepts](../explanation/concepts.md) for the
entity model and [Wire API](../reference/wire-api.md) for the
shapes, and [Environment](../reference/environment.md)
for the full `HYPHA_*` surface).

## Deeper

* [Wire API](../reference/wire-api.md) — every route
* [Architecture](../explanation/architecture.md) — planes, hub, outbox

# Build and test

**Goal:** run the same gates CI runs before pushing.

**Prerequisites:** a checkout of the repo, Rust toolchain per
`rust-toolchain.toml`, `cargo-nextest` and `cargo-llvm-cov` for the
full suite (both optional — fallbacks exist).

## Steps

```bash
cargo xtask check     # cargo fmt --check + clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings
cargo xtask test      # cargo nextest run --workspace (falls back to cargo test)
cargo xtask coverage  # cargo llvm-cov HTML report → target/llvm-cov/html
cargo xtask fmt       # apply formatting
```

The push gate (`scripts/ci.sh`, run by the peregrin ci-gate
campaign on every push): runs lint, nextest + doctests, and a
coverage check that **gates on 100% line coverage** — any
`DA:<line>,0` in the lcov report fails the build. There is no
GitHub Actions CI; run the same commands locally before pushing.

Scope a single crate while iterating:

```bash
cargo nextest run -p hypha-outbox
cargo clippy -p hypha-control --all-targets
```

## Verify

`cargo xtask check` exits 0 with no warnings; `cargo xtask test`
reports all suites green; `cargo xtask coverage` emits the lcov
report with no uncovered lines.

## Deeper

* [Architecture](../explanation/architecture.md) — which crate owns
  what before you start editing

# Read the ledger

**Goal:** know what the org is doing in this repo before proposing
or picking up work.

**Prerequisites:** `myco` installed and the `project/` worktree
present (it is — `docs/` and `project/` are git worktrees of
orphan branches created by `myco init`).

## Steps

All project state lives in the `project/` worktree via
[myco](https://github.com/9aia/myco) — tasks, backlog, issues,
proposals, plans, ADRs, handoffs. Never hand-edit files there; the
`myco` verbs are the write path.

```bash
myco status --prompt   # the board, token-sized
myco resume PL-005     # the extraction plan — briefing + handoffs
myco view board        # kanban
```

The master plan for this repo's existence is **PL-005** in the org
ledger (`9aia/workspace → repos/project`): "hypha — entity substrate
extraction from peregrin". Its handoffs carry the phase-by-phase
execution log.

## Verify

`myco status --prompt` prints the current board; `myco resume
PL-005` shows the plan's status and handoff chain.

## Deeper

* [Architecture](../explanation/architecture.md) — the planes the
  ledger's plans are building toward

# Architecture

Hypha is the *substrate* layer: distributed primitives over generic
entities. It owns who may act on an entity, when, and on which
machine — plus the transport that gets ops and snapshots there.

## Where it sits

The org stack is **delivery → memory → process → interface**.
Hypha is the **distributed substrate** — the connective layer
between nodes and workloads, at the base of the delivery layer:
the substrate that syncs entities across nodes. Integrations
(sepia's session plane, peregrin's campaigns, future
kinds) register their entity planes *on* hypha; the process layer
(`peregrin`) orchestrates campaigns on this substrate and never the
reverse; readers (`pavo`, the `hypha` CLI) read the merged index
and submit ops through the hub.

```
                 ┌─────────────── hypha-hub ───────────────┐
                 │  merged index · op routing · push · SSE  │
                 └──────────────┬───────────────┬──────────┘
                        HTTP+SSE │               │ HTTP+SSE
                  ┌──────────────▼──┐    ┌───────▼──────────┐
                  │ hypha node A    │    │ hypha node B     │
                  │ /api/entities*  │    │ /api/entities*   │
                  │ KindRegistry    │    │ KindRegistry     │
                  └───────┬─────────┘    └────────┬─────────┘
                          │  integrations register entity planes:
              ┌───────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────┐
              ▼           ▼                       ▼           ▼
        sepia-session  campaign-run          <kind-N>     entity.*
        (sepia repo)   (peregrin repo)       (any repo)   (substrate)
```

## Planes

* **Entity plane** — this repo: `EntityApi` contract
  (`hypha-node-api`), node host (`hypha serve`, `hypha-node` +
  `hypha-http`), hub gateway (`hypha-hub`), projection
  (`hypha-sync`), outbox (`hypha-outbox`), arbitration
  (`hypha-control`), push.
* **Integration planes** — one per workload kind, living in the
  workload's own repo: `sepia-peregrin` (sepia repo) registers
  `kind="sepia-session"`; peregrin registers `kind="campaign"`.
  An integration translates entity ops ↔ its verbs and implements
  snapshot as its own serialize/resume.
* **Orchestration plane** — campaigns, drivers, loaders. Stays in
  peregrin; becomes a *workload on* hypha rather than a peer of it.

## Ports and adapters

Every I/O seam is a port (`hypha-secret`, `hypha-service`, …) with
impls behind it (`-keyring`, `-dotenv`, `-systemd`). The substrate
contracts are pure — `hypha-control` has no I/O at all.

## Dataflow

Client → hub `POST /api/entities/{id}/ops` → lock gate
(`hypha-control`) → owner node `POST /api/entities/{id}/ops` → the
kind's `EntityPlane::op`. Node down? `hypha-outbox` FIFO per entity,
replayed oldest-first on reconnect. Reads merge through
`hypha-sync`'s SQLite projection + SSE diff tail.

---

---
url: /hypha/explanation/concepts.md
---
# Concepts

The whole substrate is three primitives — **entity**, **op**,
**snapshot** — plus the planes and stores around them. Get these
and the rest is plumbing.

## Entity

`{id, kind, node, indexDoc, health}`

* `kind` — free-form tag; the integration's namespace
  (`sepia-session`, `campaign`, …).
* `indexDoc` — opaque JSON for list views. Hypha merges and
  columnizes it; meaning belongs to the integration.
* `health` — liveness/lock state reported by the owner node.

## Op

`{entity, kind, payload}` — submitted to an entity's **owner node**.

* `kind` is namespaced `<integration>.<verb>` (`sepia.prompt`,
  `campaign.start`); `entity.*` is the reserved substrate namespace
  (`entity.delete` only, today).
* `payload` is opaque to hypha — the owning plane interprets it.
* Ops are idempotent-keyed and TTL'd in the outbox; `Turn`-class ops
  dead-letter on first failure.

## Snapshot

`{entity, ref, bytes}` — the migration primitive.

Serialize on the owner (`GET /api/entities/{id}/snapshot`), import on
the target (`POST /api/entities/snapshot`). Bytes are opaque
end-to-end; resume semantics are the integration's
(`campaign-snapshot/v1`, sepia session IR export, …).

## Why generic

The distributed abilities — sync, arbitration, outbox, transfer,
pairing — are orchestration-domain but workload-agnostic. Shaping
them around sessions was the mistake ADR-0091 corrected; shaping
them around *entities* is what lets CI jobs, sturn claims, or
cicada schedules become kinds without touching this repo.

## Around the primitives

* **Node** — a `hypha serve` host owning a set of entity kinds via
  its `KindRegistry`. The node is the unit of ownership: an
  entity lives on exactly one node at a time.
* **Hub** — `hypha-hub`, the aggregation gateway: merged entity
  index, op routing with offline outbox, SSE diff tail, push.
* **Owner** — the node an entity's ops route to; arbitration
  (`hypha-control`) decides who may drive entity X on node Y.
* **Outbox** — `hypha-outbox`, a durable per-entity FIFO SQLite
  queue that replays oldest-first when a node reconnects.
* **Projection** — `hypha-sync`'s SQLite entity-index + sync
  engine on the hub side; reads merge through it.
* **Kind / integration** — a workload registers `kind="<name>"`
  entities by implementing the entity-plane contract in its own
  repo (sepia's `sepia-peregrin`, peregrin's `campaign`). Hypha
  never names the kind.
* **KV** — node-local `{ns}/{key}` → JSON store (`hypha-kv` +
  `-file`) with per-namespace visibility — the generalization of
  peregrin's config/projects surface.

---

---
url: /hypha/explanation/decisions.md
---
# Decisions

ADR-lite — the decisions that shape hypha, the alternatives
rejected, and the consequence each carries. Full history lives in
the ledgers: ADR-0001 in this repo's `project/adrs/` (the
extraction), ADR-0091 in the peregrin ledger (the entity-plane
contract), PL-005 in the org ledger (the extraction plan).

## Substrate over sessions (ADR-0091)

**Decision:** the distributed layer is shaped around generic
`Entity {id, kind, indexDoc, health}` values and namespaced ops —
never around sessions or campaigns.

**Alternatives:** keep the entity plane inside peregrin shaped
around `sepia-session` (every new workload kind — CI jobs, sturn
claims, cicada schedules — would fork the substrate); a
workload-specific plane per integration (N sync/arbitration
implementations to keep correct).

**Consequence:** integrations plug in by implementing the entity
contract in their own repo; the substrate stays kind-agnostic —
no `sepia`/`campaign`/session types in these crates, enforced by
review.

## Snapshot bytes are opaque end-to-end

**Decision:** `Snapshot {entity, ref, bytes}` — serialize on the
owner, import on the target; hypha never parses the payload.

**Alternatives:** a substrate-owned snapshot schema (every
integration's state model becomes hypha's problem); references
to external stores (transfer breaks when the store is unreachable
or versioned differently).

**Consequence:** migration semantics (`campaign-snapshot/v1`,
sepia session IR) belong entirely to the integration — hypha
guarantees transport, ordering, and arbitration, nothing more.

## Ops are namespaced and TTL'd

**Decision:** op `kind` is `<integration>.<verb>` with `entity.*`
reserved for the substrate; outbox entries carry idempotency keys
and TTLs, and `Turn`-class ops dead-letter on first failure.

**Alternatives:** a flat global verb namespace (collisions across
integrations); infinite retries (a poisoned op blocks its entity's
FIFO forever).

**Consequence:** the substrate can route and dedupe without
understanding any verb; a failing op surfaces as dead-letter
instead of silent backlog.

## Policy is injected, not owned

**Decision:** `hypha-control` is a pure arbitration library —
lock registry, takeover, `pick_owner` — with no I/O; the hub
boots an empty `KindPolicies` and integrations supply policy.

**Alternatives:** policy baked into the hub (who-may-act rules
become substrate concerns); policy in each node (split-brain
arbitration).

**Consequence:** arbitration is testable pure code; orchestration
policy stays in peregrin where it belongs — the substrate decides
*mechanism*, never *intent*.

## Extracted from peregrin, composed upward

**Decision:** hypha is the entity plane lifted out of peregrin
(PL-005); `peregrin-node` becomes a thin composition root that
registers entity planes on a hypha node host.

**Alternatives:** keep the plane inside peregrin (the substrate
could never serve non-orchestration workloads); a ground-up
rewrite (the wire shapes and outbox semantics were already proven
in production inside peregrin).

**Consequence:** dependency direction is one-way —
`peregrin → hypha → ports`. Orchestration sits *on* the substrate;
the substrate never imports orchestration.

---

---
url: /hypha/explanation/boundaries.md
---
# Boundaries

Hypha sits between two neighbors and must stay generic against both.

## sepia — session *mechanism*

Sepia owns everything you can do **to** a session: attach, prompt,
restore, rewind, per-agent stores. It is deliberately just the
agent-session abstraction — it must never learn about locks,
multi-node, or orchestration.

Hypha's side of the contract: the `sepia-peregrin` adapter (which
lives **in the sepia repo**) registers `kind="sepia-session"`
entities, translates entity ops ↔ session verbs, and implements
snapshot as sepia's session IR export/import. Hypha never names a
sepia type; sepia never learns hypha exists — the adapter is the
only coupling, and it depends on hypha's public API, never the
reverse.

## peregrin — orchestration *policy + campaigns*

Peregrin owns campaigns (declarative event-driven workflows),
drivers, loaders, and policy (who may act, when, from where). Post
PL-005, peregrin's distributed layer **is** hypha: `peregrin-node`
becomes a thin composition root that registers entity planes —
`sepia-session` (via the adapter) and `campaign` (its own
`campaign_entity.rs`) — on a hypha node host.

The dependency direction is one-way:

```
peregrin (orchestration) → hypha (substrate) → ports
```

Orchestration may sit *on* the substrate; the substrate never
imports orchestration. `peregrin-hub`'s gateway role moves to
`hypha-hub`; peregrin keeps campaign verbs in its CLI.

## The rule of thumb

* "Something you do to a workload" → the integration repo.
* "Who may act on entity X, when, from where" → hypha.
* "A workflow of events and steps" → peregrin.

# Command-Line Help for `hypha`

This document contains the help content for the `hypha` command-line program.

Hypha node host — the entity substrate daemon

**Command Overview:**

* [`hypha`↴](#hypha)
* [`hypha serve`↴](#hypha-serve)

## `hypha`

Hypha node host — the entity substrate daemon

**Usage:** `hypha <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `serve` — Serve the substrate node (`/api/*`)

###### **Options:**

* `-h, --help` — Print help
* `-V, --version` — Print version

Serve the substrate node (`/api/*`)

**Usage:** `hypha serve`

# Crates

Rust workspace, ports-and-adapters. Lints are strict (pedantic warn,
`unwrap_used`/`expect_used` warn, `unsafe_code` forbid); edition
2024, rust-version 1.85.

| crate | layer | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `hypha-control` | domain | Arbitration — lock registry, takeover policy, merge/route |
| `hypha-kv` | port | Node-local key/value store port — namespaced JSON values with per-namespace visibility (P-006) |
| `hypha-node-api` | port | Node API port + wire DTOs — the hub/client ↔ node contract. NodeApi trait, ureq client, FakeNodeApi stub, rewind selector, convert targets. No leptos, no DOM. |
| `hypha-secret` | port | Secret-store port |
| `hypha-service` | port | Service-install port |
| `hypha-dotenv` | adapter | dotenv-file impl of the secret port |
| `hypha-http` | adapter | Hypha HTTP substrate — axum adapter serving /api/entities\*, /api/events, node/pairing/auth, and push over a HyphaState |
| `hypha-keyring` | adapter | OS-keyring impl of the secret port |
| `hypha-kv-file` | adapter | JSON-file impl of the hypha-kv store port — atomic tmp+rename writes (P-006) |
| `hypha-secret-cuora` | adapter | Cuora `Secrets` impl — resolves `cuora://&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;NAME&gt;` through the cuora CLI or `cuora serve` |
| `hypha-systemd` | adapter | systemd impl of the service port |
| `hypha-telemetry` | adapter | Opt-in OpenTelemetry layer over the tracing stack — OTLP export, W3C context propagation |
| `hypha-outbox` | service | Durable per-entity FIFO outbox for writes queued while a node is offline |
| `hypha-push` | service | Web Push notifications over a JSON document store — VAPID keys persist in config; subscriptions prune on 404/410 |
| `hypha-sync` | service | Hub-side sync layer — SQLite projection of paired nodes' entity indexes + outbox drain on reconnect |
| `hypha-hub` | engine | Entity-API gateway — multi-node sync engine, HTTP/SSE bridges, push, auth |
| `hypha-node` | engine | Node host — HyphaState composition + serve() for the substrate daemon |
| `hypha-serve-cli` | engine | One-shot argv→op-params shim for ndjson \*-serve binaries — the generic CLI front door (P-020). |
| `xtask` | tooling | hypha-xtask — workspace automation. |

Migration state lives in org-ledger plan **PL-005**; crate-level
API docs build via `bun run docs:api` (cargo doc →
`public/api/`).

# Environment

Hypha-native variables (landed crates):

| Variable | Crate | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HYPHA_OTEL_ENDPOINT` | `hypha-telemetry` | OTLP base endpoint; `/v1/traces` appended when no path present |
| `HYPHA_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `hypha-telemetry` | service.name (default `"hypha"`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` also honored) |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` | `hypha-telemetry` | standard OTLP vars also enable export |

Standard OTEL vars (`OTEL_*`) are honored per OpenTelemetry semantic
conventions.

Node host (`hypha serve`, `hypha-http::env::Env`):

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HYPHA_HOST` / `HYPHA_PORT` (or `PORT`) | bind address (default `127.0.0.1:18787`) |
| `HYPHA_TOKEN` | bearer auth; required on non-loopback binds |
| `HYPHA_HOME` | hypha data dir (default `~/.local/share/hypha`) |
| `HYPHA_NODE` | node identity file (default `<home>/node.json`) |
| `HYPHA_NAME` | display name on `GET /api/node` |
| `HYPHA_ORIGINS` | CORS allowlist |
| `HYPHA_SSE_KEEPALIVE_MS` | `/api/events` keep-alive cadence (`0` disables) |
| `HYPHA_PAIR_LIMIT_PER_MIN` / `HYPHA_PAIR_LIMIT_PER_DAY` | `/api/pair` throttle per client IP |
| `HYPHA_PUSH` / `HYPHA_PUSH_PATH` | push config document (default `<home>/push.json`) |
| `HYPHA_KV` / `HYPHA_KV_PATH` | node-local KV document for `/api/kv*` (default `<home>/kv.json`) |

Hub (`hypha-hub`, `hypha_hub::HubConfig` + `hub_state_from_with`):

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HYPHA_HUB_HOST` / `HYPHA_HUB_PORT` (or `HYPHA_PORT`) | bind (default `127.0.0.1:13000`) |
| `HYPHA_HUB_TOKEN` | client→hub auth; required on non-loopback binds |
| `HYPHA_NODE_URL` / `HYPHA_NODE_TOKEN` | single-node upstream shorthand |
| `HYPHA_NODES` | `id=url[@token];…` multi-node registry |
| `HYPHA_HOME` | hub data under `<home>/hub/` (projection, outbox, push, credentials) |
| `HYPHA_CREDENTIAL_STORE` | `auto`/`keyring`/`file` node-token backend |
| `HYPHA_EPHEMERAL_DEAD_AFTER` | seconds; ephemeral-node reap window (default 300) |

Both binaries (`hypha serve`, `hypha-hub`) initialize the same OTEL
layer — the `HYPHA_OTEL_*`/`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` vars above apply to
each process.

url: /hypha/reference/wire-api.md
---
# Wire API

The entity-plane HTTP surface — served by the node host
(`hypha-http`), aggregated by the hub (`hypha-hub`). One canonical
spelling per route: `hypha-node-api`'s `HttpEntityApi` and the hub
speak the same paths. (The P3-era alias spellings —
`/api/entities/{id}/export`, `/api/entities/import`, `/api/index`,
`/api/outbox` — are gone.)

## Node surface

| Route | Verb | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/health` | GET | liveness probe (pre-auth) |
| `/api/pair` | POST | redeem a pairing code → bearer token |
| `/api/auth/login` `/api/auth/logout` | POST | auth-cookie exchange |
| `/api/user` | GET | OS user info for pickers |
| `/api/node` | GET/PATCH | node descriptor / rename |
| `/api/fs?path=` | GET | direct subdirectories of an absolute path |
| `/api/events` | GET | SSE event feed |
| `/api/entities` | GET/POST | list (`?kind=`) / create entity |
| `/api/entities/{id}` | GET/DELETE | entity doc / `entity.delete` |
| `/api/entities/{id}/ops` | POST | submit op `{kind, payload}` |
| `/api/entities/{id}/snapshot` | GET | export snapshot bytes |
| `/api/entities/snapshot` | POST | import snapshot (`body.kind` picks the plane) |
| `/api/entity-index` | GET | `{"index": [{node, entities}]}` — one row, this node |
| `/api/pending-ops` | GET | `{"ops": [...]}` — always empty on a bare node (the outbox is hub-side) |
| `/api/kv` `/api/kv/{ns}` `/api/kv/{ns}/{key}` | GET (+ PUT/PATCH/DELETE on the key) | node-local KV — `{ns}/{key}` → JSON, per-namespace `public`/`internal` visibility (default `<home>/kv.json`) |
| `/api/client/keypair` | POST | mint a stateless Ed25519 client keypair (node-side, for non-secure contexts) |
| `/api/push/vapid` | GET | `{publicKey}` (501 without a push store) |
| `/api/push/subscribe` | POST/DELETE | push subscription add/remove |

## Hub surface

Same `/api/entities*` shape, aggregated: merged index from all
`HYPHA_NODES` nodes, ops routed to the owner (durable outbox when
offline), plus hub-owned routes:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/entity-index` | merged per-node entity buckets |
| `/api/node-status` | `{"nodes": [...]}` — per-node liveness: `status` (`unknown`/`up`/`down`), `lastSeenAt`, `downSince` (first observed failure), `ephemeral` (self-reported disposable lifecycle) |
| `/api/pending-ops` | outbox depth — queued + dead-letter ops |
| `/api/events` | SSE bridge to the upstream node |
| `/api/entities/{id}/stream` | per-entity live stream (kind policy's `stream_path`, owning node) |
| `/api/push/*` | hub-owned subscription store (fans out to every node) |
| `/api/{*rest}` | passthrough to the upstream node for everything else |

Not on the substrate: `/api/config*` — node config is
integration-owned (a composing integration mounts its own surface);
`EntityApi::get_config`/`set_config` are doc-hidden for that reason.

### Node lifecycle

The sync engine tracks each registered node on the projection's
`nodes` row: `status` moves `unknown → up` on a successful
subscribe+list and back to `down` on any failed cycle (reconnects
retry forever at capped exponential backoff). `downSince` stamps the
first observed failure and clears on reconnect. Merged entity lists
carry the owner's status inline as `nodeStatus`, so a dead node's
stale index entries are distinguishable from live ones; ops to a
down node queue durably in the hub outbox and replay on reconnect.

A node whose `GET /api/node` `capabilities` include `"ephemeral"`
(e.g. `peregrin serve --ephemeral` CI runners) is treated as
disposable: once it has been continuously `down` for
`SyncOptions::ephemeral_dead_after` (default 5 min) the engine drops
its projected entities — a resurrected node resyncs itself — and
dead-letters its queued writes rather than letting them pend
forever. The `nodes` row stays, so `/api/node-status` keeps reporting
`down` + `ephemeral`.

## Client

`hypha_node_api::HttpEntityApi` (ureq) implements `EntityApi`;
`FakeEntityApi` is the in-memory test double. Wire DTOs:
`EntityDto`, `EntityOp`, `EntityIndexDto`, `PendingOpDto`,
`NodeInfoDto`, `NodeStatusDto`, `PushSubscriptionDto` — see
`hypha-node-api/src/dto.rs` and the generated rustdoc under
`/hypha/api/`.
